item.title: Springboks must find answers to All Blacks’ breakdown pressure
item.description: Springboks halfback Cobus Reinach says South Africa must find a way to deal with New Zealand’s pressure at the breakdown and produce quicker ball if they are to win the second Test in Cape Town. The All Blacks beat the Springboks 33-16 in the opening Test in Johannesburg, moving to the top of the World Rugby rankings.
item.content:encoded:
Springboks halfback Cobus Reinach says South Africa must find a way to deal with New Zealand’s pressure at the breakdown and produce quicker ball if they are to win the second Test in Cape Town.

The All Blacks beat the Springboks 33-16 in the opening Test in Johannesburg, moving to the top of the World Rugby rankings.

South Africa had several chances inside the New Zealand 22 but managed only one try as handling errors and strong defence from the All Blacks kept the hosts under pressure.

The Springboks were also reduced to 13 men late in the match after Reinach and another player were sent to the sin-bin.

Reinach says New Zealand’s pressure forced South Africa into mistakes.

He says the Springboks must learn from the defeat and find better ways to handle the All Blacks’ defence.

All Blacks will face South Africa this Sunday at 3am in Cape Town.

item.title: 120 schoolgirls to be assessed for higher-level rugby competition
item.description: 120 schoolgirls will be observed over three days as part of a programme aimed at strengthening Fiji’s women’s rugby development pathway and preparing more players for higher-level competition. Former Black Fern and current Hurricanes Women’s coach Mel Bosman is in Nadi as part of the Impact Beyond Pasifika Programme, which is funded by the Australian Government in partnership with World Rugby.
item.content:encoded:
120 schoolgirls will be observed over three days as part of a programme aimed at strengthening Fiji’s women’s rugby development pathway and preparing more players for higher-level competition.

Former Black Fern and current Hurricanes Women’s coach Mel Bosman is in Nadi as part of the Impact Beyond Pasifika Programme, which is funded by the Australian Government in partnership with World Rugby.

Insert: Bosman on support womens rugby 27th Aug 26

She says secondary school coaches from the North, South, East and West are taking part, with the programme focusing on session planning, teaching skills and helping coaches better develop young players.

Bosman says it is important to empower coaches and give them the confidence to develop strong relationships with young female players.

She says young girls need to believe they are good enough to play rugby, and coaches have an important role in building that confidence and creating an environment where players trust what they are being taught.

Bosman, who is a former Black Fern, has also coached in the United States women’s rugby programme and is now part of the Hurricanes Women’s coaching team.

She says she had the opportunity to watch the secondary schools Under-18 girls’ final in Suva on Saturday and was impressed by the potential and talent on display.

Bosman says it was exciting throughout the 70 minutes, with the coaches watching impressed by the players’ ability to keep the ball alive, kick and chase, use space and express themselves on the field.

Bosman says this could eventually help players progress through to the Fijiana 7s, Fijian Drua Women and Fijiana 15s programmes.

She adds that programmes of this nature are not available everywhere, saying even New Zealand does not currently have a similar programme in place for women and girls.

Bosman says being part of the programme in Fiji will also allow her to learn from Fiji’s approach and take that experience back to New Zealand to explore how player development programmes there can be further strengthened.

item.title: Fijian Drua sign Nadroga centre Kavekini Boselawa
item.description: The 21-year-old caught the eye of Drua head coach Brad Mooar with his physicality, versatility and potential, earning him a place in the club’s development pathway. Boselawa only began playing rugby at 19 after previously playing soccer at Nadrala Sangam School and Sigatoka Methodist College.
item.content:encoded:
The 21-year-old caught the eye of Drua head coach Brad Mooar with his physicality, versatility and potential, earning him a place in the club’s development pathway.

Boselawa only began playing rugby at 19 after previously playing soccer at Nadrala Sangam School and Sigatoka Methodist College.

He later represented Nadrala Rugby Club and Nadroga.

Boselawa who hails from Naduri, Macuata, says he was grateful and emotional after signing his first contract with the Drua.

Mooar says Boselawa immediately stood out during the Skipper Cup match in Lautoka and praised his potential.

The signing highlights the Drua’s commitment to developing local talent and creating pathways from Fiji’s domestic competitions to Shop N Save Super Rugby Pacific.

Boselawa now hopes to continue developing his game and earn an opportunity to represent the Drua in front of Fiji’s passionate home supporters.

item.title: Navua eyes Extra BOG glory as 21-year title drought continues
item.description: Navua FC will head into the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants hoping to end a 21-year wait for their second BOG title. The Southerners last lifted the trophy in 2005 when the Gurjit Singh-coached side defeated Rewa 1-0 in the final in Suva.
item.content:encoded:
Navua FC will head into the 2026 Extra Battle of the Giants hoping to end a 21-year wait for their second BOG title.

The Southerners last lifted the trophy in 2005 when the Gurjit Singh-coached side defeated Rewa 1-0 in the final in Suva.

While Navua have experienced the joy of winning the tournament once, they have also endured heartbreak, finishing runners-up on three occasions.

They lost 2-1 to Suva in the 1995 final, before Rewa defeated them 1-0 in 2010.

Their most recent appearance in the final came in 2023, when Labasa beat them 2-1 after extra time.

With another opportunity now ahead, Navua will take the field at Four R Stadium, Govind Park in Ba hoping to add a second BOG title to their history.

Head coach Roderick Singh has stressed the importance of consistency as the side prepares for the tournament.

Rewa to face Champions Ba face in final Extra Premier League match
item.description: Rewa will be looking to end their 2026 Extra Premier League campaign on a high when they take on newly crowned champions Dayal's Sawmillers Ba this Saturday. The Delta Tigers are guaranteed to finish third on the points table after going down to Prithvi Navua by 1-0 last weekend, which left them on 32 points.
item.content:encoded:
Rewa will be looking to end their 2026 Extra Premier League campaign on a high when they take on newly crowned champions Dayal's Sawmillers Ba this Saturday.

The Delta Tigers are guaranteed to finish third on the points table after going down to Prithvi Navua by 1-0 last weekend, which left them on 32 points.

Ba has already secured the league title , while Extra Supermarket Labasa has confirmed second place.

For the Men in Black, Saturday's match will be an opportunity to celebrate their championship-winning season in front of their home supporters after ending a seven-year wait for the national league title.

The match will also give both teams valuable competitive preparation ahead of the Extra Battle of the Giants, which kicks off the following weekend at the same venue.

Rewa faces Ba at Four R Stadium, Govind Park Ba at 3pm on Saturday.

Meanwhile, Extra Battle of the Giants will kick start from 4th of next month also in Ba.
